description:
FILED s507 (Fable, 2026-10-04) from the review probes of s506f (perl's switches in `pcl`): the one-liner `perl -ne 'print "$ARGV:$.:$_"; close ARGV if eof' f1 f2` is this bug, and it is in the RUNTIME, not in the switch handling -- the same loop as a FILE on main:

  f1 = "a\nb\n", f2 = "c\n";   while (<>) { print "$ARGV:$.:$_"; close ARGV if eof }
  perl:  f1:1:a  f1:2:b  f2:1:c
  PCL :  f1:1:a  f1:2:b  f2:3:c          (main 2e71d4aa and the s506f tree alike)

perl's rule (perlfunc eof / close): an explicit `close` resets `$.`; the IMPLICIT close when <> moves to the next file does not -- which is exactly why the idiom exists.  Probe both halves: without the `close ARGV`, perl prints f2:3:c too.
Fix site: p-close on the ARGV handle (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) -- the line counter of the magic ARGV stream; check what an explicit `close $fh` on an ordinary handle does to `$.` today (perl: reset when that handle is the last-read one).
BREAKING CASES: `eof` vs `eof()` (the last file); `$.` after the loop ends; `close ARGV` followed by more `<>` reads continuing with the next file; `-i` in-place editing (the same ARGV machinery, s506f's `-i.orig` rows).
Probe files: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s507/review/sw.pl case `files-eof`, tmp/x/w.pl.


=== DONE (s507b, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-04) ===
`(p-close ARGV)` found no handle (the <> stream lives in *p-argv-stream*, not the handle table) and answered "".
Now %p-close-impl routes the bareword ARGV (%p-argv-handle-p, the same spelling test as the <> marker) to
%p-close-argv: close the current file, reset its $. and the cumulative seed, answer 1; the next <> opens the next
@ARGV file.  An in-place edit stays the selected output until the next file opens (perl's ARGVOUT) -- %p-inplace-
finish moved to the top of the "open the next file" step (a first try that committed it at the close sent -p's last
line to STDOUT).  Also perl's IOf_START: a LATER pass of <> over a refilled @ARGV counts from 1 again.
Probes scratch/s507b/m4/ar.pl (the idiom, $. after the loop, a second pass, close mid-file then more reads) and
ip.sh (-i.bak -pe with close ARGV, -ne numbering) identical to perl except `eof()` WITH parens, PRE-EXISTING and
filed #2703 (PCL emits (p-eof) for both spellings).  Guard Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t row 92 (fails on 08de9e4f).
subject: SILENT WRONG (found by a s507 review probe, PRE-EXISTING on main 2e71d4aa): `close ARGV` does not reset `$.` -- perlfunc's own idiom `while (<>) { print "$ARGV:$.:$_"; close ARGV if eof }` numbers the second file's lines on from the first's (perl: each file from 1)
